title: URL shortener: create and open a short link
goal: Understand how a short link is created in a web form, how a visitor opens it, which parts are frontend, backend, and infrastructure, what is stored where, and what happens when the short code does not exist. This is a planned design. Nothing is built yet, and the use of a cache is not decided.

includes: Creating a short link from a web form
Opening a short link and receiving a redirect
The not-found path for a short code that does not exist
excludes: Click analytics and counts (planned, not designed)
Custom short codes chosen by the user (planned, not designed)

groups.label: Frontend
groups.description: What the user and the visitor see in the browser.

groups.label: Backend
groups.description: Server code that creates and resolves short links.

groups.label: Infrastructure
groups.description: Storage, optional cache, and network routing.

components.label: Web form
components.summary: A form where a user pastes a long URL and asks for a short link. Planned, not built.

components.label: Visitor browser
components.summary: Opens a short link and follows the redirect to the long URL. Planned, not built.

components.label: Create endpoint
components.summary: Receives the long URL, gets a short code, saves the pair, and returns the short link. Planned, not built.

components.label: Short code generator
components.summary: Makes a new short code for each long URL. Planned, not built.

components.label: Redirect handler
components.summary: Looks up a short code and answers with a redirect, or with a not-found response. Planned, not built.

components.label: Link store
components.summary: Durable storage of short code and long URL pairs. The database type is not chosen. Planned, not built.

components.label: Cache (not decided)
components.summary: An optional fast copy of recent short codes. Whether it exists is not decided. Planned, not built.

components.label: Domain and routing
components.summary: Routes requests for the short domain to the redirect handler. Planned, not built.

items.text: It is not decided whether to use a cache. The redirect path works without one, and the cache is shown only as an option.
Which database type should hold the short code and long URL pairs?
How are short codes made, and what happens when two long URLs would get the same code?
When the short code does not exist, should the visitor see a not-found page or be sent to another page?
Should the redirect use a temporary or a permanent status code? Browsers may store permanent redirects for a long time.
The material does not say whether short links expire.
Users paste complete web addresses that start with http or https.

scenarios.title: Create a short link
scenarios.summary: Planned design. A user turns a long URL into a short link through the web form.

steps.caption: The user pastes a long URL into the web form and submits it.
The create endpoint asks the code generator for a new short code.
The create endpoint saves the short code and the long URL in the link store.
The form shows the new short link to the user.

scenarios.title: Open an existing short link
scenarios.summary: Planned design. A visitor opens a short link and is redirected to the long URL.

steps.caption: The visitor opens the short link in the browser.
The domain routing passes the request to the redirect handler.
The handler checks the cache first, if a cache exists.
On a cache miss, the handler reads the long URL from the link store.
The handler sends a redirect, and the browser opens the long URL.

scenarios.title: Open a short code that does not exist
scenarios.summary: Planned design. This is the not-found path. The response shape is not decided.

steps.caption: The visitor opens a short link whose code was never created.
The domain routing passes the request to the redirect handler.
The handler finds no matching code in the cache or the link store.
The handler returns a not-found response, and its exact form is not decided.
